answer: One Sybil defense is a bonded identity registry with quadratic weighting. Each agent locks a crystal bond in a garden of identities; voting power grows only with the square root of that stake. An audit, cold as a glacier, randomly reopens accounts and slashes the bond of any cluster shown to be one actor split into many. Splitting a fixed budget across fake names buys no extra influence, since power tracks the root of stake, not headcount, while every fake account must post its own bond. To gain sway, an attacker must lock more capital, and the random audit makes duplicates a losing bet.
